{"questions":[{"id":"p1","kind":"path","question":"The first print call passes two separate strings: console.print("Hello", "World!", style="bold red"). Which Console method turns those two arguments into renderables, how many renderables come out, and what is the resulting content?","key":"Console._collect_renderables (rich/console.py:1500) handles it. Each str goes through Console.render_str (markup render + ReprHighlighter), producing two Text objects that are accumulated in the local `text` list; check_text() then joins them with Text(sep) where sep=" " (Text.join), so exactly ONE renderable is returned: a Text whose plain value is "Hello World!" (no spans, since ReprHighlighter matched nothing). The style "bold red" is not applied here — it is applied later in Console.print via Segment.apply_style.","lines":["rich/console.py:1500-1587","rich/text.py:778-815"],"check":"import io

from rich.text import Text

assert r[0].spans == []
"},{"id":"p2","kind":"path","question":"For the README table printed on a 100-cell console, what is Table._extra_width, what width is passed to _calculate_column_widths, and what list of column widths comes back?","key":"_extra_width is 5 (2 for the box edges because box is set and show_edge is True, plus len(columns)-1 = 3 column dividers). __rich_console__ therefore calls _calculate_column_widths with options.update_width(100 - 5) = 95, and it returns [14, 35, 19, 16] (Date is a fixed width=12 column + 2 padding; Title is 33 for "Star Wars Ep. VIII: The Last Jedi" + 2; Production Budget is the 17-char header + 2; Box Office is 14 for "$1,332,539,889" + 2). Total table width = sum(widths) + extra_width = 84 + 5 = 89, which fits in 100 so no collapsing happens.","lines":["rich/table.py:295-303","rich/table.py:475-495","rich/table.py:523-586"],"check":"import io
from rich.console import Console
from rich.table import Table
c = Console(record=True, width=100, file=io.StringIO())
t = Table(show_header=True, header_style="bold magenta")
t.add_column("Date", style="dim", width=12)
t.add_column("Title")
t.add_column("Production Budget", justify="right")
t.add_column("Box Office", justify="right")
t.add_row("Dec 20, 2019", "Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker", "$275,000,000", "$375,126,118")
t.add_row("May 25, 2018", "[red]Solo[/red]: A Star Wars Story", "$275,000,000", "$393,151,347")
t.add_row("Dec 15, 2017", "Star Wars Ep. VIII: The Last Jedi", "$262,000,000", "[bold]$1,332,539,889[/bold]")
assert t._extra_width == 5
widths = t._calculate_column_widths(c, c.options.update_width(100 - t._extra_width))

"},{"id":"p3","kind":"path","question":"The Console was built with the default color_system="auto". Which color system was detected in this run, why, and what does that mean for the text that reaches the file?","key":"Console._detect_color_system returned None: is_jupyter is False, and `self.is_terminal` is False (the output file is not a tty and no FORCE_COLOR/TTY_COMPATIBLE env var is set), so the `if not self.is_terminal or self.is_dumb_terminal: return None` branch is taken. console._color_system is None / console.color_system is None. In _render_buffer each segment's Style.render is called with color_system=None, and Style.render returns the text unchanged when color_system is None — so although "bold red" was requested, no ANSI SGR escape sequences are written and the exported text contains no \x1b characters.","lines":["rich/console.py:789-811","rich/style.py:694-718","rich/console.py:2132-2154"],"check":"import io

"},{"id":"p4","kind":"path","question":"When the Text "Hello World!" is wrapped for a 100-cell console, divide_line is called. "},{"id":"p5","kind":"path","question":"Inside Console.print, because style="bold red" was given, a different branch is taken than for a styleless print. Which branch, and exactly which Segments end up in the (record) buffer for this call?","key":"Because `style is not None`, print takes the else-branch: it resolves the style with Console.get_style("bold red") -> Style(color=red, bold=True), then iterates Segment.split_lines_terminator(render(renderable, options)) and applies Segment.apply_style(line, render_style) per line, appending a bare Segment.line() ("\n", no style) after each terminated line. The buffer therefore holds exactly two segments: Segment('Hello World!', Style(color=Color('red'), bold=True)) and Segment('\n', None). crop=True so split_and_crop_lines runs with pad=False, which leaves the 12-cell line unpadded on the 100-cell console.","lines":["rich/console.py:1729-1756","rich/segment.py:186-225","rich/segment.py:275-304"],"check":"import io

"},{"id":"p6","kind":"path","question":"The very first Segment produced when the table is rendered is the box top. "},{"id":"g1","kind":"general","question":"What does Console.export_text/export_html/export_svg guarantee about recording, how is the precondition enforced, and what happens on a second call?","key":"Exporting only works if the Console was constructed (or set) with record=True; segments are copied into _record_buffer in _write_buffer only when record is True and _buffer_index is 0. The precondition is enforced with a bare `assert self.record, "To export console contents set record=True in the constructor or instance"` — an AssertionError, which is silently skipped under `python -O`, in which case the export simply returns empty/degenerate content instead of failing. All export methods default to clear=True, so the record buffer is emptied after exporting and a second call returns only what was printed since; export_text(styles=False) also drops control segments and all styles.","lines":["rich/console.py:2192-2222","rich/console.py:2059-2066","rich/console.py:2268-2270"],"check":"import io

"},{"id":"g2","kind":"general","question":"In what order does Console.is_terminal decide whether the output device understands escape sequences, and which environment variables can override auto-detection?","key":"Order in Console.is_terminal: (1) explicit force_terminal (self._force_terminal) wins; (2) Idle is special-cased to False (sys.stdin.__module__ starting with 'idlelib'); (3) Jupyter returns False; (4) TTY_COMPATIBLE == "0" -> False, "1" -> True; (5) FORCE_COLOR, if set at all, returns (value != ""), i.e. any non-empty value forces True and an empty value forces False; (6) otherwise file.isatty(), with a ValueError from a closed file caught and turned into False. is_dumb_terminal additionally requires is_terminal and TERM in ("dumb", "unknown"). This matters because is_terminal drives color system detection, alt-screen/cursor control and window-title writes.","lines":["rich/console.py:930-988"],"check":"import io
from rich.console import Console
f = io.StringIO()
assert Console(file=f, _environ={"TTY_COMPATIBLE": "1"}).is_terminal is True
assert Console(file=f, _environ={"TTY_COMPATIBLE": "0", "FORCE_COLOR": "1"}).is_terminal is False
assert Console(file=f, _environ={"FORCE_COLOR": "1"}).is_terminal is True
assert Console(file=f, _environ={"FORCE_COLOR": ""}).is_terminal is False
assert Console(file=f, _environ={}, force_terminal=True).is_terminal is True
assert Console(file=f, _environ={}).is_terminal is False
"},{"id":"g3","kind":"general","question":"Console markup is enabled by default. How can user-supplied text be mis-rendered or raise, and what is the supported way to print literal square brackets?","key":"Any string printed with markup enabled is parsed by rich.markup.render: a tag-looking fragment matching RE_TAGS (`[` followed by a-z, #, / or @) is consumed as a style tag, so arbitrary user data can silently lose text or change styling. A closing tag with no matching open tag raises MarkupError ("closing tag ... doesn't match any open tag"), and '[/]' with an empty stack raises MarkupError too; a bad @-handler parameter also raises MarkupError. Unclosed open tags are not an error — they are auto-closed at the end of the text. The supported fix is rich.markup.escape(), which doubles backslashes and inserts a backslash before the bracket (render later turns '\\[' back into '['), or passing markup=False to print/render_str.","lines":["rich/markup.py:12-70","rich/markup.py:153-231","rich/console.py:1437-1460"],"check":"from rich.markup import render, escape
from rich.errors import MarkupError
ok = False
try:
    render("[/red]")
except MarkupError:
    ok = True
assert ok
t = render("[bold]x")
assert t.plain == "x" and t.spans[0].style == "bold"
assert render(escape("[bold]")).plain == "[bold]"
"},{"id":"g4","kind":"general","question":"What are the rules of Table.add_row when the number of cells does not match the number of columns, or when a cell is not renderable?","key":"add_row pads a short row with None values up to len(columns), and each None becomes an empty string cell. If more renderables are given than there are columns, a new Column is appended on the fly (with highlight taken from the table) and back-filled with Text("") for every existing row, so earlier rows stay aligned. Each cell must satisfy protocol.is_renderable (a str, or an object with __rich__ / __rich_console__); anything else raises errors.NotRenderableError("unable to render <type>; a string or other renderable object is required"). Finally a Row(style=..., end_section=...) is appended, so rows and column cell lists are kept in step.","lines":["rich/table.py:422-467","rich/protocol.py:9-15"],"check":"from rich.table import Table
from rich.text import Text
from rich.errors import NotRenderableError
t = Table("A", "B")
t.add_row("1")
assert list(t.columns[1].cells) == [""]
t.add_row("1", "2", "3")
assert len(t.columns) == 3
cells = list(t.columns[2].cells)
assert isinstance(cells[0], Text) and cells[0].plain == "" and cells[1] == "3"
ok = False
try:
    t.add_row(object())
except NotRenderableError:
    ok = True
assert ok
"},{"id":"g5","kind":"general","question":"Under which conditions does Rich silently swap the box style you asked for, and how can that be disabled?","key":"Box.substitute(options, safe) swaps boxes twice: if options.legacy_windows and safe is True it looks the box up in LEGACY_WINDOWS_SUBSTITUTIONS (ROUNDED/HEAVY/HEAVY_EDGE/HEAVY_HEAD -> SQUARE, MINIMAL_HEAVY_HEAD -> MINIMAL, SIMPLE_HEAVY -> SIMPLE); and if options.ascii_only (i.e. the console encoding does not start with 'utf') and the box is not already ascii, it is replaced by box.ASCII regardless of `safe`. Table passes safe=pick_bool(self.safe_box, console.safe_box) (both default True), so setting safe_box=False on the Table or Console disables only the legacy-Windows substitution — the ascii_only fallback cannot be turned off. Separately, when show_header is False the box is replaced by get_plain_headed_box() (e.g. HEAVY_HEAD -> SQUARE).","lines":["rich/box.py:67-93","rich/box.py:405-421","rich/table.py:766-774","rich/console.py:142-145"],"check":"from rich import box
from rich.console import ConsoleOptions, ConsoleDimensions
ascii_opts = ConsoleOptions(size=ConsoleDimensions(80, 25), legacy_windows=False, min_width=1, max_width=80, is_terminal=False, encoding="ascii", max_height=25)
assert ascii_opts.ascii_only is True
assert box.ROUNDED.substitute(ascii_opts) is box.ASCII
assert box.ROUNDED.substitute(ascii_opts, safe=False) is box.ASCII
legacy = ConsoleOptions(size=ConsoleDimensions(80, 25), legacy_windows=True, min_width=1, max_width=80, is_terminal=False, encoding="utf-8", max_height=25)
assert box.ROUNDED.substitute(legacy, safe=True) is box.SQUARE
assert box.ROUNDED.substitute(legacy, safe=False) is box.ROUNDED
assert box.HEAVY_HEAD.get_plain_headed_box() is box.SQUARE
"},{"id":"g6","kind":"general","question":"What does Console do with buffered output when quiet=True, and what is the default behaviour when writing raises BrokenPipeError or UnicodeEncodeError?","key":"_check_buffer is the single gate: if self.quiet is True the whole buffer is discarded (`del self._buffer[:]`) and nothing is written — note that recording happens inside _write_buffer, so a quiet console records nothing either. Otherwise _write_buffer runs; a BrokenPipeError is caught and routed to Console.on_broken_pipe(), whose default implementation sets quiet=True, redirects stdout's fd to os.devnull and raises SystemExit(1) (subclasses may override this). A UnicodeEncodeError is re-raised after appending the hint '*** You may need to add PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8 to your environment ***' to error.reason. On Windows the writer also chunks output into <= 32*1024//4 character writes to avoid the CPython 32Kb write bug.","lines":["rich/console.py:2030-2057","rich/console.py:2059-2130"],"check":"import io

c = Console(file=f, quiet=True, width=20, record=True)

assert c.export_text() == ""
"},{"id":"g7","kind":"general","question":"How does Console.get_style resolve a name, and what happens for an unparseable style name?","key":"get_style returns the argument unchanged if it is already a Style; otherwise it first looks the name up in the thread-local ThemeStack (theme styles such as 'table.header', 'log.time'), and only if that misses does it call Style.parse on the string. Style.parse treats 'none'/empty as the null style and otherwise accepts attribute words, 'not <attr>', 'on <color>' and 'link <url>', raising errors.StyleSyntaxError for anything it cannot parse as a color. get_style converts that into errors.MissingStyle(f"Failed to get style {name!r}; {error}") unless a `default` was supplied, in which case the default is resolved instead. Styles carrying a link are returned as a copy (so each use gets a fresh link id); Style.parse and Style.normalize are lru_cached (4096/1024 entries).","lines":["rich/console.py:1470-1498","rich/style.py:496-561","rich/theme.py:81-111"],"check":"import io
from rich.console import Console

assert c.get_style("table.header") == c._theme_stack.get("table.header")
assert c.get_style(Style(bold=True)) == Style(bold=True)
ok = False
try:
    c.get_style("not_a_color")
except MissingStyle:
    ok = True
assert ok
assert c.get_style("not_a_color", default="bold") == Style.parse("bold")
"}]}
